scope: Frozen observer and smoke evidence only. No process snapshots, hooks, gates, Git commands, configuration changes or observer changes were performed for this review.

smoke.assessment: All nine recorded processes were baseline cmd.exe children directly parented by 10588. No bash/python/git process, new spawn, exit, or CIM query was recorded. This is a smoke test of direct-child sampling only, not a test of MSYS fork/exec ancestry completeness.

code_findings.finding: Selection uses Toolhelp32 Win32 PID/parent PID snapshot, not CIM ancestry. is_descendant returns false as soon as an intermediate PID is absent from the current rows and not in ancestors.

Already tracked exited ancestors are removed before new-process discovery. The ancestor set retains only the original live root and live tracked allowed executables. No historical ancestry ledger is retained.
CIM role queries are queued only for processes already selected by ancestry. They cannot recover a candidate omitted by the ancestry filter.

Selected processes have creation-time identities, but intermediate parent links are traversed by numeric PID alone; PID reuse remains a potential false attribution unless parent/child creation times are checked in a future ancestry ledger.

The existing completion receipt correctly states short-lived process and late orphan omissions. Absence of a gate/git process in this trace cannot establish that it finished or that a pipe writer was absent.

conclusion: Yes: if an intermediate Windows process exits before a discovery poll, a surviving gate or git descendant can be missed, even if its own lifetime is long. A removed formerly tracked parent also loses its link. The smoke trace does not establish that an actual gate child was missed, and does not establish a frequency or the cause of the current timeout.

parent_report_not_independently_sampled.statement: Parent reports a current normal POSIX gate exceeding 60 seconds with active MSYS git diff PID9096, approximately 36 CPU seconds and 95 MB read, and is testing native/MSYS index-cache interactions.
parent_report_not_independently_sampled.qualification: This review did not inspect that active process or rerun its command. Substantial reported CPU/IO motivates the parent investigation independently of this observer completeness finding.

safe_additive_correction_proposals: Preserve observe.py and smoke-01. If a new observer is authorized, maintain a bounded historical ancestry ledger for every observed descendant node, including intermediate executable names outside the recorded target allowlist. Bind nodes to creation FILETIME, retain observed exit times, check parent-before-child time ordering and reject PID-reuse ambiguity. Continue recording detailed CPU/IO only for the authorized target executables.
Historical tracking improves observed-parent exits but cannot recover an intermediate process born and gone entirely between polls. Do not advertise polling as complete process-creation tracing.

For a practical narrow fallback, accept explicitly supplied additional watch PIDs only with independently supplied/validated creation FILETIME and exact expected executable path. Record them as explicitly watched processes with ancestry unconfirmed unless separately established; never silently classify them as root descendants. This allows a known gate/git PID to remain observable across missing intermediate ancestry without collecting unrelated system processes.

If complete creation coverage is necessary, a separate authorized process-creation event trace or cooperative PID marker may be considered. Neither was implemented or run here. Do not broaden discovery to every system Python/Git process or capture raw environment/command lines.
